newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Cricket-Victoria to bat against Shield leaders Queensland.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-Victoria to bat against Shield leaders Queensland.

text.p: Stand-in Victoria captain Dean Jones won the toss and decided to bat against Sheffield Shield leaders Queensland in their match at the Gabba on Friday.

Jones, who had led the Victorians for three years before being replaced by Shane Warne earlier this year, was named captain this week after an injury to Tony Dodemaide. Warne is playing for Australia in the second test against West Indies in Sydney.
Victoria named Graeme Vimpani as 12th man while Queensland left out Jimmy Maher in favour of spin bowler Paul Jackson.
The Victorians have not had an outright win in a Shield match in Brisbane since the 1964-65 season.
All-rounder Andrew Symonds has recovered from a virus and will play for Queensland, who are without test players Ian Healy and Michael Kapsrowicz.
Queensland lead the Shield standings after outright wins in their first two matches.
Teams:
Victoria - Warren Ayres, Michael Foster, Dean Jones (captain), Brad Hodge, Laurie Harper, Ian Harvey, Darren Berry, David Saker, Brad Stacey, Brad Williams, Troy Corbett.
Queensland - Matthew Hayden, Trevor Barsby, Martin Love, Stuart Law (captain), Geoff Foley, Andrew Symonds, Wade Seccombe, Andrew Bichel, Adam Dale, Scott Muller, Paul Jackson.
In Adelaide, South Australia won the toss and chose to bat in their match against Western Australia.
South Australia were boosted by the return of leg-spinner Peter McIntyre, who was overlooked by national selectors after earlier being named in a 13-man Australia second test squad.
Western Australia were boosted by the return of pace bowler Jo Angel from injury and Adam Gilchrist and Brad Hogg from recent representative duties.
Teams:
Western Australia - Mark Lavender, Mike Hussey, Justin Langer, Damien Martyn, Tom Moody (captain), Brendon Julian, Adam Gilchrist, Jo Angel, Brad Hogg, Ryan Campbell, Matthew Garnaut.
South Australia - Jamie Siddons (captain), Adam Kimber, Ben Johnson, Darren Lehmann, James Brayshaw, Geoff Parker, Joe Scuderi, Tim Nielsen, Peter McIntyre, Shane George, Mark Harrity.
In Hobart, New South Wales won the toss and decided to bat in their match against Tasmania.
Spinner Stuart MacGill was left out of the New South Wales side while pace bowler Andrew Saballus was omitted by Tasmania.
Teams:
New South Wales - Michael Slater, Brad MacNamara, Kevin Roberts, Rodney Davison, Corey Richards, Greg Matthews (captain), Phil Emery, Shane Lee, Phil Alley, David Freedman, Anthony Stuart.
Tasmania - Dene Hills, Mark Atkinson, David Boon (captain), Michael DiVenuto, Jamie Cox, Tony Daly, Daniel Marsh, Colin Miller, Mark Ridgway, Shaun Young, John Saint.
